items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: My mom had records. I can remember listening to — she had an Ahmad Jamal record

ctx.x: Did you have a moment growing up that you can recall where the music really made an impression on you and led you down this path?

Well I was playing violin at a young age, like three or four, the Suzuki method of classical music and stuff. And I grew up in St. Louis, and I was lucky enough to grow up in an area, University City, well the Cleetown first and then U City, and like some of the guys a little older than me were playing jazz. Like Todd Williams played with Wynton Marsalis, and Peter Martin plays piano with Diane Reeves, and Chris Thomas, a great bass player. And Todd was in Wynton’s band, so this was probably like the late 80s. So…
You were just going to be a —
